tell: A selective NaV1.8 blocker whose major active metabolite, M6-SUZ, is 3.7-fold less potent than the parent.

clues.text: Food lowers early concentrations without changing overall exposure. It is 99% protein bound and cleared mainly through CYP3A metabolism.
A white to off-white solid, practically insoluble in water, with a molecular weight of 473.39 g/mol.
Approved under an NDA in a single 50 mg tablet strength. The first dose is 100 mg, and the second dose is 50 mg.
No boxed warning; contraindicated with strong CYP3A inhibitors. Pruritus and muscle spasms are the most common adverse reactions compared with placebo.
Moderate to severe acute pain, including postoperative pain, in adults.
A selective blocker of the NaV1.8 voltage-gated sodium channel in peripheral sensory neurons, which stops pain signals reaching the spinal cord and brain.
The generic name begins with S and has eleven letters.
